title: Leveraging Large Language Models to Measure Gender Representation Bias in Gendered Language Corpora

model.params_source: assumed = API defaults: the authors' released validation notebook calls chat.completions with only model and messages, so temperature 1.0 / top_p 1.0 were in force; the paper's F-score 90.24% +/- 0.55% over five runs confirms that sampling was on. max_tokens assumed (the answer is a short word list).

task.subset_rule: all 100 manually annotated Spanish Europarl sentences of the validation set (Appendix C)
task.approximation: 3 harness seeds instead of the paper's 5 runs. The released notebook is parameterised for gpt-4o-2024-11-20; the model id is set to the snapshot Table 4 names as the selected model (gpt-4-turbo = gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 per Sec. 4.2). Everything else - prompt pattern, five priming examples, skip list, answer parser, count definitions and the pooled F-score - is the authors' own released code.

items.source: https://github.com/ellisalicante/grb-corpora, file data/validation/gt-es.txt (100 sentences with word-level ground truth), with data/dataset-analysis/skiplist-es.txt for the ignored pronouns
items.config_or_split: the Spanish validation set (gt-es.txt); gt-va.txt is the Valencian counterpart (F-score 84.43%)
items.license: see LICENSE.txt in the repository; the source sentences are Europarl (public)

fields_source.input: the quoted sentence of each block
fields_source.label: the quoted annotation block, upper-cased, split into [WORD, P/N, M/F] triples and filtered through the skip list

files: gt-es.txt (28,862 bytes, 100 sentences, 686 annotated words after the skip list)

download.note: 100 blocks parsed, 686 gold word triples after skip-list filtering

prompt.user_template:
Ejemplo 1: "El señor Presidente viajó a Tokio para reunirse con el secretario de estado y a la mañana siguiente tuvo que volar a Madrid por temas personales."

Ejemplo 4: "El Sr. Johnson, un respetado colega de la ciudadanía británica, ha vivido en Londres durante más de dos décadas, donde trabaja incansablemente para mejorar la comunidad local."
Sr. - P, M

Ejemplo 5: "Encontré en Europa no solo destinos turísticos, sino un hogar temporal donde me sentí ciudadana del mundo, abrazando la diversidad y la riqueza cultural que esta tierra ofrece."
Europa - N, F

Frase: "{sentence}"

Instrucciones: Identifica todos los sustantivos y pronombres en la frase proporcionada. Para cada uno, determina si se refiere a una persona (P) o no (N), y especifica su género gramatical: masculino (M), femenino (F). Excluye los apellidos. Sigue el formato de los ejemplos proporcionados sin añadir texto adicional.
prompt.few_shot: k=5 fixed examples, printed in Table 3 of the paper and released as data/dataset-analysis/examples-es.txt; they are substituted into the <EXAMPLES> slot exactly as the released notebook does
prompt.source_location: Appendix A (prompt formulation) and Appendix B / Table 3 (the five priming examples); the byte-exact strings are the repository files data/dataset-analysis/prompt-es.txt and examples-es.txt
prompt.verbatim: full. Two harmless differences between Appendix A's typeset version and the released prompt file are resolved in favour of the file that the code actually loads: the file writes the sentence in quotes (Frase: "<SENTENCE>") and lists the genders as 'masculino (M), femenino (F)' where the appendix prints 'masculino (M) o femenino (F)'. The system message 'You are a helpful assistant.' comes from the notebook.

output.postprocess:
hook parse() = parse_response() of the released notebook: strip, upper-case, collapse ' 
', split on ' - ', ', ' and newlines, regroup in threes, drop groups whose word is in the skip list

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: F-score = 2PR/(P+R) with P = nc/(nc+ni+ne) and R = nc/(nc+nm), where nc = words correctly identified and correctly classified on both attributes, ni = identified but at least one attribute wrong, nm = missed, ne = extra; counts pooled over the 100 sentences (Appendix C)
metric.original_location: Table 4, row gpt-4-turbo, column F-score (%) = 90.24 +/- 0.55 (accuracy 89.40, precision 89.53, recall 90.96); also quoted in Sec. 4.2
metric.bootstrap_unit: sentence (set-level resample: pooled F-score recomputed on resampled sentences)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run --cap 20 on 2026-09-19: 100 items x 3 seeds = 300 calls, ~156k input tokens (the five priming examples ride along in every call).

open_points: The paper averages five runs at the API default temperature; the harness runs three seeds, so seed-to-seed spread is expected to be of the order of the paper's +/- 0.55 pp.
notes: The claim cell is a validation-set capability number for the annotator model, not a downstream corpus statistic. The Valencian counterpart (gt-va.txt, F 84.43%) uses the same pipeline with the translated prompt and examples. gpt-4o-2024-05-13 (84.65) and gpt-4-0125-preview (87.04) appear in the same table; the latter is a dead snapshot.
